result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B is the more finished and memorable logo. Its drop sits on a drill bit above creek waves, and the green, gold and blue palette suits a rural trade well. It loses points for using a generic circle badge, a fairly plain bold sans wordmark, and having no single flat-color version. A covers more of the rubric, with one-color, reversed and 16–32px versions, and its heavy stacked wordmark is chosen with care. But its mark is mostly a stock water drop, and there is an awkwardly large gap between the mark and the name. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): A's badge combines a drop, a drill bit and creek waves, so it ties the mark to drilling and to the place. Its forest green, gold and blue palette also suits a rural trade, and the logo is the clear focus of the page. B is more thorough with variants: it shows a true one-color version and 32px and 16px sizes. But its mark is close to a stock water drop with a thin line, and the large gap between icon and wordmark weakens the lockup.
